name: CAPE VERDE

flag.title: Cabo Verde Flag
flag.note: Blue seas, red-white path, ten island stars

lead: Ten volcanic islands in the Atlantic, 570 km off West Africa. Nobody lived here until Portuguese sailors arrived in 1460 — so every person and song is a blend of Africa, Europe, and the sea. Today Cape Verde is one of Africa's most stable democracies, famous for surf, nesting sea turtles, and a soulful music called morna.

sections.geography: A land of fire & desert winds

geo: Cape Verde's ten islands split into two groups: the flat, sandy eastern islands — Sal and Boa Vista — where wind sculpts endless dunes, and the rugged western islands — Santo Antão and Fogo — where jagged peaks plunge into the sea.

The biggest wow is Fogo island: an active volcano last erupted in 2014 and buried a whole village in lava. Farmers now grow coffee and grapes inside the crater — one of the world's most dramatic vineyards.
animals: Cape Verde has one of the world's largest loggerhead turtle nesting colonies — over 170,000 nests in a single season on Boa Vista's beaches. Each August, mother turtles haul ashore by night to lay eggs in the warm sand.

The Raso lark survives only on one tiny uninhabited islet — the whole species would fit inside a football stadium. Humpback whales pass through in winter and five turtle species swim in Cape Verdean waters.
culture: Cape Verdean culture blends African rhythm with Portuguese melody. Morna — a slow, soulful music of longing and sea — was added to UNESCO's intangible heritage list in 2019. Cesária Évora, the 'Barefoot Diva' from Mindelo, carried it to concert halls worldwide.

Food reflects the same blend: cachupa is a national stew of corn and beans simmered with fish or meat — every family has its own recipe. Mindelo throws one of Africa's most colourful carnival parades each February.
history: Before 1460 the islands were completely empty. Portuguese explorers built a colony that became West Africa's first major trading hub, linking Europe, Africa, and the Americas — and, tragically, a key stop in the transatlantic slave trade.

For 500 years Cape Verde was Portuguese. Leader Amílcar Cabral inspired the independence movement, and freedom was won without a battle — through negotiation after Portugal's 1974 revolution. Independence Day: 5 July 1975.
wows: Cape Verde has no rivers — most islands get fresh water entirely from desalination plants.
Cesária Évora's face appears on the 2,000 escudo note — rare for a musician on currency.
Pico do Fogo erupted in 2014; people moved back and farm inside the lava field today.
Cape Verde has never had a military coup — remarkable stability in the region.
Trade winds blow so hard on some islands that trees grow permanently sideways.
More Cape Verdeans live abroad than on the islands — a global diaspora of musicians & fishers.
In the 1800s Mindelo was one of the Atlantic's busiest coaling stops for steam ships.

myths.myth: Cape Verde is just a beach destination
myths.fact: The islands also have active volcanoes, cloud-forest hikes, windsurfing, endemic birds found nowhere else, and a vast sea-turtle nesting ground.
Portuguese is official for writing, but virtually all Cape Verdeans speak Kriolu — a creole blending Portuguese with West African languages — as their real mother tongue.
